Conditions zuint signals

Source: R/conditions.R
zuint-conditions.Rd

Every error and warning zuint raises has a class, which is part of its interface and safe to test for; the message text is not. Each also has the class zuint_error or zuint_warning.

Details

Errors:

  • zuint_type_error: an argument of the wrong kind.

  • zuint_incompatible_error: two types with no common type, such as int128 and uint128 (see zu_common_type()).

  • zuint_double_error: a double that is not integral or not in range, in arithmetic, comparison-free mixing or c(); see options(zuint.double).

  • zuint_overflow_error: a result out of range under a checked_*() function (see checked_add()).

  • zuint_division_error: a zero divisor in checked_idiv() or checked_mod().

  • zuint_arrow_error: an Arrow array zuint cannot read, or a released struct (see zu_from_arrow()).

  • zuint_unsupported_error: an operation zuint does not do, such as quantile() or a matrix.

Warnings:

  • zuint_cast_warning: values that could not be represented became NA.

  • zuint_overflow_warning: a result out of range became NA.

  • zuint_precision_warning: a conversion to double rounded.

  • zuint_double_warning: a double was computed in double, under options(zuint.double = "allow").

  • zuint_recycling_warning: operand lengths are not multiples.

  • zuint_empty_warning: min() or max() of nothing.

Examples

tryCatch(int128(1) + uint128(1), zuint_incompatible_error = function(e) "no common type")
#> [1] "no common type"
withCallingHandlers(int64(1.5), zuint_cast_warning = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
#> <int64[1]>
#> [1] NA
